own_tests.input: DINOv2-small CLS cosine nearest field_train neighbour for each of the 1040 field_dev images (CPU), views of the closest 32 pairs and 16-pair samples per source in the 0.9+ and 0.8-0.9 bands
own_tests.result: Cosine >=0.95: 16 images, nearly all the same photo or crop (mirror/crop/watermark variants). >=0.90: 72 images (40 plantdoc, 32 plantseg); by eye about 45-50% of the plantdoc ones and about 75% of the plantseg ones are the same photo or same scene, so roughly 40 of 1040 field_dev images (about 4%) are real look-alikes of a field_train image that survived dedup. 0.80-0.90 band: 322 images, mostly different photos of similar subjects (stock-series leaves, similar lesions), a few (~10%) same-scene.

own_tests.input: convnext_joint field_dev accuracy / macro-F1 with images removed at DINO cosine cutoffs (own macro-F1 code; full set 0.7644 / 0.7653)
own_tests.result: remove >=0.95 (16): 0.7617 / 0.7628; >=0.90 (72): 0.7552 / 0.7592; remove only same-label >=0.90 pairs (62): acc 0.7536; >=0.85 (205): 0.7329 / 0.7478; >=0.80 (394): 0.6950 / 0.7225; >=0.70 (840): 0.6300 / 0.6426. The last rows remove mostly non-duplicate easy look-alikes, so they are a pessimistic bound. Thumbnail-correlation (32px, 4 flips) finds only 5 images at >=0.90 and 50 at >=0.80, with kept macro-F1 0.7631 and 0.7614.

own_tests.input: Accuracy with vs without a close field_train neighbour
own_tests.result: Near images are easier: plantdoc cos>=0.9 acc 0.850 vs 0.737 for the rest (n 40/579); plantseg 0.938 vs 0.781 (n 32/389). Accuracy rises monotonically over neighbour-similarity quartiles (0.658, 0.692, 0.823, 0.885) but this is also the effect of ordinary visual similarity (the label of the nearest neighbour equals the true label for only 65% of images), not only copying. Even in the lowest band (cos<0.8) joint accuracy is 0.655 plantdoc and 0.748 plantseg, versus E1's ~0.22.

own_tests.input: Is the held-out gap leakage or source shift? Joint vs held-out accuracy by neighbour similarity band
own_tests.result: The gap is large where there are no look-alikes: plantdoc cos<0.8 joint 0.655 vs held-out 0.375 (gap 0.28); plantseg cos<0.8 0.748 vs 0.432 (gap 0.32). On cos<0.9 it is 0.307 and 0.249, against overall gaps 0.312 and 0.247. Near-duplicate images are only ~4% of dev, so they cannot produce a 25-31 point gap. Better explained by ordinary source shift plus the loss of about half the real training data (plantdoc 0 of 1227, or plantseg 0 of 842, rows), not by leakage.

own_tests.input: Style cues that leak class within a source
own_tests.result: PlantSeg has 0 healthy images, so within real photos 'healthy' is only learnable from PlantDoc/lab. In PlantDoc field_train, white-background stock-style images (border mean >235, 12% of images) are 92.5% healthy versus 26% for the rest, spread over 18 classes; model accuracy on dev white-bg images is 0.842 (n 76) vs 0.731 for the rest. This is a real dataset-style cue that favours dev, but it is modest in effect and is shared by field_dev because the splits are random by group. Filenames/folders are not model inputs (pixels only).

E1 never saw a real photo; joint training puts 2069 real photos into training, so a large jump is expected. My leakage measure moves the joint number by at most 1 point of macro-F1 at the plausible duplicate level (0.7653 -> 0.7592 removing all 72 at >=0.9) and still 0.7225 removing 394 images at >=0.8, so the jump is real, with the caveat that the dev numbers are optimistic.

notes: Leakage reading: the 0.765 holds. About 40 of 1040 field_dev images (4%) are same-photo or same-scene look-alikes of a field_train image that dedup missed (consistent with the docs' stated limit); they are scored about 0.89-0.94 accurate. Removing every image with a >=0.9 neighbour moves accuracy by about 1 point (0.7644 to 0.7552) and macro-F1 by 0.6 points (0.7653 to 0.7592). The held-out gap (0.732 to 0.378 plantdoc, 0.775 to 0.518 plantseg) persists on images with no look-alike (0.28 and 0.32 accuracy gaps), so it reflects source shift and the loss of half the real training data, not leakage. Residual risks to report, not failures: (1) the plantdoc white-background stock style is 92% healthy, and PlantSeg has no healthy class, so some of the within-source skill is style, which will not transfer to phone photos; (2) selection and arm choice use field_dev, so numbers stay optimistic (the records say so); (3) the 'noise' backgrounds in the background arm are garish rather than natural, which is a design weakness not a defect; (4) differences among arms 1 to 4 (0.746 to 0.765) are within what a single seed could produce, since only one seed was run and no interval across arms 1-4 was checked by me; (5) the crop arm uses E10 masks trained on PlantSeg only. Prediction jsonl files list PlantDoc image paths, like earlier records, but contain no image content. My scratch work (embeddings, montages) is in orchestration/evidence/tmp-T4.1/. I did not compute anything on field_test.
